preamble: Fortition of the lateral approximant [l] to the voiced alveolar lateral fricative [ɮ] adds turbulent airflow while keeping the lateral channel. The clearest historical case is Khalkha Mongolian, where Proto-Mongolic *l became a fricative /ɮ/ (often devoiced to [ɬ]) while Chakhar kept [l]; in Yami (Tao) of Orchid Island, /l/ is realized as [ɮ] before the high front vowel /i/.

examples.note: Khalkha has no lateral approximant; the inherited lateral is a voiced lateral fricative /ɮ/, frequently realized voiceless [ɬ]. Chakhar Mongolian retains [l] in the same word (/tʃil/).
The fricative lateral occurs in all positions in Khalkha.
/l/ becomes the voiced lateral fricative [ɮ] before high front /i/; under Mandarin contact, younger and Mandarin-dominant speakers are reverting this to [l].

sources: Svantesson, J.-O., Tsendina, A., Karlsson, A., & Franzén, V. (2005). The Phonology of Mongolian. Oxford University Press. https://global.oup.com/academic/product/the-phonology-of-mongolian-9780199260171
